intents.text: Add a `max_body_size` keyword option (default `None`, meaning unlimited as today) to `Starlette`, `Router`, `Mount` and `Route`.
The application-level limit applies before routing, and a limit on an inner route, mount or router overrides the outer one for that part of the tree, whether it raises or lowers the outer limit.
Provide `RequestBodyLimitMiddleware(app, max_body_size=...)` in `starlette.middleware.body_limit`, working with any ASGI application and not only Starlette.

Enforce the limit on the body bytes actually received from the ASGI server (multipart file data and encoding overhead included), so an absent or understated Content-Length does not let an oversized body through.

Reject a declared Content-Length over the limit before any application code runs: in Starlette, once routing has settled the applicable limit (matched route's own, else the outer one, else the app's for no-route or no-method matches); in the standalone middleware, on entry.

A request exceeding the limit gets a 413 response with the plain-text body `Content Too Large`; if the application has already started its response, no second response is sent and the body stream is stopped.
Multipart parsing closes its temporary files whenever a parse is interrupted, including when the body limit is crossed.
Requests without a body, websockets and lifespan are unaffected by the limit.
Document the `max_body_size` option and `RequestBodyLimitMiddleware` in the project docs.

Add tests covering the limit on app, router, mount and route (including an inner limit raising and lowering the outer one), the standalone middleware, Content-Length fail-fast, the multipart case and temp-file cleanup.

constraints: Default None must keep today's unlimited behaviour.
The existing test suite must stay green.
